main_text.p: Horrendum stridēs, flammisq; armata Chymera, Gorgones, Harpiaq;, & forma tricorporis umbrae, phantasmata, quibus nihil respondere in re fatebitur, opinor: etiam in huiusmodi visis magnas formas agnoscat est necesse, nisi Briareum centum manibus praeditum, capitibus quinquaginta, cujus magnitudinem mirantur In theogon.[?]a Hesiodus & De orig. Deor. lib. 1.b Apollodorus, pusionem fuisse dicet: Mortuorum denique spectra & umbras, aut pares, aut majores corporibus, quorum speciem referunt, apparere, testatur apud eundem Aeneid. lib. 2.c Virgilium Æneas:

p.i: Infelix simulacrum, atque ipsius umbra Creusae Visa mihi ante oculos, & nota maior imago.

main_text.p: Quumadmodum & Vlyffes apud Odyss. lib. ii.d Homerum describit Achillis umbram ingenti passu gradientem: & Apollonius Tyaneus eandem, e tumulo I [illegible, ~12 letters](ut scribit De vita Apollon. lib. 4. cap. 5.e Philostratus) excitatam, ait sibi vi-sam statura primo quinque, postea duodecim qua-si cubitorum. Quamobrem ex tanto cum Graecorum autorum consensu, tum Latinorum, in quibus & eorum quos profe producit acerrimus adversarius, patet formam omnem idolo significari: ac proinde εἴδωλον neutiquam deduci per diminutionem a vocabulo εἶδος. Nimirum derivatur a verbo εἴδω, quod sonat videri, aut assimilari; ut ἴωλος ab ἔω, φειδωλὸς à φειδω, ἐυχωλὴ ab ἐυχω[?]: sicut Etymolog. mag. in vocabulis, εἰδῶλον, ἔωλος, & ἐυχωλή. [illegible, ~20 letters]f diligentissimus etymologiarum Graecarum observator ex recepta εἰδώλω significatione colli-git similiúmque vocum analogia firmat. Itaque ut idem significant ἐυχωλὴ & ἐυχὴ, παυσωλὴ & παῦσις[?], φειδωλὸς & φειδὸς; nec alterum alterius diminutivum est, sed ambo sunt ex eodem fonte, εὐχέσθαι, παυέσθαι, φειδέσθαι: sic εἴδωλον & εἶδος,

page.notes: Right margin: the marginal notes are a–f as keyed to the text marks. Note "I" with Greek beside the Apollonius passage and the Greek notes beside the etymology are illegible and transcribed as placeholders. The Greek in the text is a best reading: the accents, the ω/ε/υ letters in ἐυχωλὴ, παυσωλὴ and φειδωλὸς, and the final word of the Greek lines are doubtful. The mark "z" after "significatione" has no matching note on the page as far as I can see. "profe producit" and "pusionem" are copied as printed. The first two lines are in italics and the rest of the paragraph is roman. The page number 545 is printed in an old form (long s style) and may be misread.
